messages:
lucy: seeing a spike in 404s for old doc anchors after the MDX migration. lots of links like /api/auth#login -> now go to /api/auth#login-1 or missing entirely
rafael: hmm that sounds like duplicate heading ids got deduped differently by remark-slug and our emoji strips. did we add the remark-autolink plugin in the migration?
erin: i did add remark-autolink to get link icons, but I also enabled a transform that removes emoji from headings which changes the slug. that would explain it
lucy: right. a concrete example: the page `guides/auth.md` had heading `## Login 🚀` before, slug used to be `login-` (emoji ignored) but new slug becomes `login-1` because the cleaner removed emoji earlier in pipeline. old anchors from other pages now 404
chris: we have a handful of internal references and external customer links to those anchors. need a strategy: either restore previous slug behavior or add redirects for affected anchors
rafael: adding redirects on CDN for every anchor is painful. better to make remark-slug deterministic and match our historical behavior. there should be a config flag to preserve ascii-only slug generation or to remove dedupe suffixing
erin: i found that remark-slug builds ids after other remark transforms. if we move emoji-strip earlier (pre-slug) it will produce the old id. quick patch in docs pipeline could reorder plugins
lucy: okay do that, but we should also generate a compatibility redirect map for the top 30 most-hit anchors (from analytics) just in case
docs-bot: action required: docs build failed on preview branch at step: build-mdx (error: duplicate id "login-1"), see https://ci.redwood.ai/8456
chris: duplicate id error probably because two headings both normalize to same slug after emoji strip. the old pipeline tolerated duplicates and append -1 -2 differently. we need to replicate prior dedupe logic or fix content to have unique headings
rafael: plan: (1) erin reorders remark plugins so slugifying matches old behavior, (2) lucy will grep for headings that would still collide and open small wording fixes, (3) i will produce an anchor redirect map and a Netlify/CloudFront rule for the top anchors
erin: I'll open a tiny PR to reorder plugins and add a test that runs `yarn docs:build` and asserts stable slugs for a fixture file. PR: https://github.com/redwood-ai/docs/pull/4201
lucy: i'll run a grep: `rg "^##" docs | sed -E 's/^##+ //' | tr -d '\r' | slugify-script > tmp/slugs-before.txt` and compare with the fixtures. i'll post any collisions in the PR comments
chris: also let's add a quick linkcheck job that follows in-page anchors (not just page-level HTTP checks). we had that in the past but it was disabled for speed. enable it for the preflight run at least
docs-bot: note: enabling full anchor-check will add ~30s to docs CI. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
rafael: acceptable tradeoff for stability. once we confirm the plugin reorder works, we can run a staging rebuild and check analytics for 404s
erin: i made the plugin reorder change and added a unit test. pushing draft now. also added a note in migration doc about emoji handling in headings: docs/migration/mdx-emoji-slugs.md
lucy: thanks. i fixed two headings that would have collided and opened PR https://github.com/redwood-ai/docs/pull/4202 with edits and screenshots showing before/after slugs
chris: i'll prepare the redirect map. can you generate a CSV of old -> new anchors from analytics? lucy, can you dump the top 50 anchor 404s?
lucy: yes grabbing from GA and CloudFront logs now, will post in the PR comments
rafael: once PRs are green, we can do a staged deploy tomorrow 04:00 UTC and monitor site 404s for 45m. if anything odd, rollback. also inform the support team about potential broken customer bookmarks
lucy: pinged support + links channel. also added a short FAQ snippet to top of migration docs explaining why slugs changed and where to report broken anchors
docs-bot: CI update: preview build 8460 queued, ETA ~8m.
